query: What should I do if my car won't start?
generated_text:
If your car won't start, let's go through some steps to diagnose the issue. First, check if the dashboard lights come on when you turn the key. If they don't, it's likely that the battery is dead. In this case, you can try jump-starting your car. Make sure to follow the proper jump-starting procedure to avoid any damage to the electrical system.

If the dashboard lights do come on, but the car still won't start, it could be a problem with the starter motor or the fuel delivery system. Check if the engine cranks when you turn the key. If it does, but the car won't start, it might be a fuel or spark issue. 

For your 2020 Corolla, it's also a good idea to check the fuel pump and ignition system. A faulty fuel pump or ignition coil could be preventing the car from starting. 

If you're not comfortable diagnosing the issue yourself, it's always best to consult a professional mechanic. They can inspect the ignition and fuel systems to determine the root cause of the problem and recommend the necessary repairs.

Remember to prioritize your safety and the safety of others on the road. If you're unable to start your car, make sure to move it to a safe location and turn on the hazard lights to alert other drivers.

query: How do I check my car's oil level?
generated_text:
To check your car's oil level, make sure the vehicle is parked on a level surface and turned off. Let it sit for a few minutes to allow the oil to drain back into the oil pan. Locate the oil dipstick, which is usually labeled "Oil" or have an oil can symbol on it. Pull out the dipstick and wipe it clean with a lint-free cloth or paper towel. Insert the dipstick back into the oil reservoir and pull it out again. The dipstick will now be coated with oil, and the oil level will be indicated by the oil's level on the dipstick. 

Check the oil level against the minimum and maximum marks on the dipstick. If the level is below the minimum mark, you'll need to add oil. Be sure to use the type of oil recommended by the manufacturer, which can be found in your owner's manual. 

It's also a good idea to check the oil color and consistency. If the oil is dark or dirty, it may be a sign that it's time for an oil change. If you're unsure about any aspect of the process or notice any issues, it's always best to consult a professional mechanic for guidance. 

In your case, since your car is a 2020 Corolla with a petrol engine, you can refer to the owner's manual for specific instructions on checking the oil level, as the location of the oil dipstick and the recommended oil type may vary. However, the general process remains the same.
reference_text: To check your oil level, park the car on level ground and wait for the engine to cool down. Pull out the dipstick, wipe it clean with a rag, insert it all the way back in, and then pull it out again. The oil level should be between the 'Full' and 'Add' (or 'F' and 'L') marks.
